correctness.rationale: For the explicit tail law, \(T_k=T_{k-1}^4\) and \(p_k=T_{k-1}-T_k\) are exact. At \(N_k=T_k^{-1}\), no value exceeds level \(k\) with probability tending to \(e^{-1}\), while the level-\(k\) multiplicity is asymptotic in mean to \(N_k^{3/4}\), so two independent maximizing sets intersect with probability tending to one on an event of probability \(e^{-2}\). At \(M_k=T_{k-1}^{-3/2}\), each coordinate maximum equals \(k\) with probability tending to one, but the probability of any common level-\(k\) index is at most \(M_k p_k^2\to0\). These bounds prove the displayed liminf and limsup claims without extrapolating from finite computations.

value.rationale: The motivating literature proves \(a_n\to0\) under a regularity condition and asks about arbitrary infinite-support independent marginals. The construction gives a mathematically natural boundary phenomenon: without regular tails, leader probabilities can have order-one peaks while still having zero troughs. This identifies a genuine obstruction to convergence-based approaches to the conjecture and quantifies it with an explicit \(e^{-2}\) peak lower bound, rather than supplying an arbitrary finite example.
